newsitem.title: USA: FOCUS-Valero buy propels it to big leagues.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Valero buy propels it to big leagues.

text.p: Valero Energy Corp's $485 million purchase of Salomon Inc's Basis Petroleum unit propels it into the top five ranks of independent refiners, at a time when the only way to survive in a tight industry seems to be through size.
The industry is divided between those like Salomon, which sold $3.0 billion of assets for cents on the dollar, and the likes of Valero and Tosco Corp, who are aggressive buyers.

"We are buying for less than ten cents on the dollar... We had a window of opportunity to buy at a discount at a time when we think the cycle is going to improve," Valero chief executive Bill Greehey told a teleconference on Monday.

Basis has spent over $650 million on its refineries -- two in Texas and one in Louisiana -- since 1992 and some $300 million of assets were placed in service late last year. Greehy said these had not yet been reflected in Basis earnings.
Analysts were very bullish on the impact of Valero's addition of 300,000 barrels per day (bpd) of refining capacity, which will give Valero a total of 500,000 bpd once the deal is completed on May 1.

"I had a price target of the high $30 for Valero's stock before the acquisition; after it, that target looks more like $40 plus, as Basis will start contributing very soon," said Ravi Kamath, refining and marketing analyst at Jefferies & Co.
Valero stock moved up 3/4 to 33-1/2 by midafternoon.
The company is making the acquisition through a mixture of stock and cash and is close to finalizing the terms of a $250 million syndicated loan to help finance the deal.
"Even after this, our debt to capital ratio will be under 30 percent, which is very comfortable," said Danny Gibbons, Valero's vice president finance.

Valero said that the Basis purchase would not affect its plans to spin off its refining and marketing business to a separate company and merge its natural gas related services business with PG&E Corp.

The Basis deal widens Valero's product line, with 100,000 barrels per day of distillate and 10,000 bpd of chemical grade propylene. The deal also offers synergies with its existing 171,500 bpd Corpus Christi, Texas, refinery and Salomon has agreed to let Valero participate in feedstock and operating decisions immediately, said Baines Manning, vice president refining at Valero.

"This should allow us to get part of our own feedstock in place, make some changes to the configuration of the refineries and make the operation profitable immediately," said Valero vice president of refining Baines Manning.

Valero plans to reduce overhead at the Basis refineries by $26 million and plans just one major upgrade at the Texas City, Texas, refinery, which at $50 million has a payback time of less than 10 years.
Commenting on the outlook for Valero's earnings, CEO Greehey said that he was comfortable with analysts' estimates of earnings per share in the low 30 cents.

"We are seeing an improvement in the refining cycle; margins continue to be north of six dollars but gas and liquid earnings will be less than they were in the first quarter of 1996 -- but that was a record quarter for gas," Greehey said.
Greehey said that Valero would keep an eye on further acquistions but would absorb Basis first and analysts believe that size is the only way to survive in refinining.

"There is still no pricing power in this industry, so the only way to improve margins is by being bigger. We will see a lot more merger and acquisition activity in this sector," said Ravi Kamath of Jefferies. ((-- David Chance New York Newsroom 212 859 1902))
